final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the indispensable catalytic lysine that forms the Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; substitution with alanine abolishes cofactor binding and eliminates enzyme activity.
G307 is a conserved active-site loop residue; introducing a bulky charged aspartate severely disrupts active-site conformation and completely abolishes CBS activity.
Charge reversal at the catalytic K119 position creates electrostatic repulsion against cofactor binding and completely destroys PLP-dependent catalytic competence.

stop_reason.detail: Targeting the essential catalytic Schiff-base lysine and active-site architecture provides clear, conclusive loss-of-function candidates.

history.rationale: Lys119 forms the essential Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; mutation to Ala eliminates PLP binding and abolishes catalytic activity.
K119 is the catalytic lysine forming the Schiff base with PLP; mutating to Ala directly destroys catalytic competence with very high predicted pathogenicity (0.987).
Charge inversion at the catalytic PLP-binding Lys119 prevents cofactor coordination and completely inactivates the enzyme.
Charge reversal at catalytic K119 severely impairs PLP binding and catalytic function, supported by a 0.974 pathogenicity prediction.
G307S is a canonical pathogenic homocystinuria mutation known to cause complete loss of CBS catalytic activity.
Classic homocystinuria mutation with high pathogenicity (0.828), though slightly less disruptive than G307D.
The most prevalent homocystinuria mutation, I278T disrupts active core folding and severely compromises enzyme activity.
Predicted benign (0.159) by AlphaMissense; clinically responsive to pyridoxine, likely retaining significant residual catalytic activity.

rejection.reason: Predicted benign (0.159) by AlphaMissense; clinically responsive to pyridoxine, likely retaining significant residual catalytic activity.

history.rationale: Introducing a charged aspartate into the tightly packed G307 turn disrupts local active site conformation, abolishing function.
G307D exhibits the highest pathogenicity score (0.992) and 0% representation in MSA, strongly indicating complete loss of function.
T191M is a well-characterized severe homocystinuria allele that impairs active site integrity and causes loss of function.
Moderately high pathogenicity (0.716), consistent with clinical CBS deficiency phenotypes.
Cys52 serves as an axial ligand for heme binding; removing the coordinating thiolate impairs heme binding and CBS stability/function.
C52 is an axial heme ligand essential for normal CBS assembly and regulation, with high pathogenicity (0.951) despite some MSA tolerance.
His65 is the secondary axial heme iron ligand; substitution disrupts heme coordination and impairs enzymatic competence.
Phenotype tool indicates ambiguous pathogenicity (0.480), making complete activity loss less certain.
Thr146 is situated in the conserved active site loop adjacent to the PLP pocket; alanine mutation impairs substrate catalysis.
Active site threonine substitution has solid pathogenic prediction (0.788).
Arg125 is an active-site adjacent residue mutated in homocystinuria that destabilizes the catalytic pocket.
Predicted benign (0.153) by AlphaMissense, unlikely to reliably abolish enzymatic activity.
